title: I made a Pocket God style game with Claude from my phone. Looking for playtesters (how I made it + token cost inside)
author: superpikapoo
selftext:
I've been building a pocket god like game with Claude for about a week and it's at the point where I need people to play it and tell me what's broken.

It's called Isle of Ages. You're the god of a small island. You can help your tribe grow from hunter gatherers all the way to the space age, or you can wreck them with lightning, meteors, tornadoes, volcanoes, dragons etc. Powers can be combined into combos (there's 26 to find). You earn divinity to unlock a power tree that's pretty heavy on wrath, and different endings unlock new islands like a frozen one, a desert one, a volcanic one and Mars.

Link: 

Free, plays in the browser, no sign up. Made for phones but works on desktop too.

How I made it

I did the whole thing from my phone in the Claude app and didn't write any code. My first prompt was:

"Build a pocket god like game in 3js. I want realistic graphics, so water, shaders, sand, power animations, and a working eco system, a progressive civilization starting from hunters and gathers going to modern and future."

After that it was basically play it on my phone, tell Claude what was broken or what I wanted next, repeat. Around 20 versions so far. Claude works in its own workspace so it writes the code, tests it and updates the same link each time. For bigger updates it split the work between sub agents (15 total, up to 6 at once) and merged everything after. It even made the trailer by recording the game frame by frame and editing it with ffmpeg.

The tech stuff since people always ask

\- three.js loaded from a CDN plus 2 Google fonts. That's the only outside stuff

\- No models, textures or sound files. Everything is made with code, the 3D models, the water/sand/sky shaders, even the sound effects

\- About 43,000 lines of JavaScript in 81 files that get built into one 2.9 MB HTML file

\- The game simulation can run without graphics, so Claude runs 1,144 checks plus UI tests before every update

Tokens and cost

I'm on a subscription so this isn't what I actually paid, but I had Claude work it out at API prices (Opus 5.5).

The last stretch (playtest prep and the trailer) was measured: about 44M cached tokens read, 0.36M written to cache and 0.16M output. Roughly $15.

The whole week is an estimate since it can't see all of it: around 2 billion tokens (almost all cheap cached re-reads) and about 10M output. Somewhere around $500-1,000 at API prices.

Stuff that helped

\- Have it build tests early. They caught most bugs before I ever saw them

\- Be specific with feedback. "The daily tasks never update past day 1" got fixed right away

\- Ask it for ideas and just pick the ones you like. I asked how to get people to keep coming back and replied with the numbers I wanted

What I want feedback on

1. First 5 minutes, did anything confuse you?

2. Best power or combo?

3. Would you come back and play again tomorrow? Why or why not?

4. How did it run on your device?

5. Bugs: Settings > Report a problem > Copy, then paste it in the comments

It's a playtest so the balance isn't done and I'm sure there's bugs. Any feedback helps, and questions about the process are welcome too.
